name: Face Warping Artifact
algorithm: Face Warping Artifact — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method detects geometric warping artifacts in face-swap deepfakes:

1. **Face Geometry Analysis**: The 3D face geometry is estimated from 2D landmarks per frame. Face-swap methods warp the source face to match the target's geometry using affine or 3D morphable model transforms. Residual geometric artifacts from imperfect warping are detected.

2. **Warping Distortion Detection**: Local geometric distortion is measured by analyzing: (a) unnaturally stretched or compressed facial regions, (b) non-uniform scaling inconsistent with perspective projection, (c) barrel/pincushion distortion not matching the camera's lens model. These warp residuals indicate face replacement.

3. **Facial Proportion Consistency**: Key facial proportions (eye width/face width, nose length/face length, lip width/inter-ocular distance) are measured across frames. Natural proportions remain constant (bone structure doesn't change). Warping artifacts may cause subtle proportion fluctuations as the face swap adjusts to varying target poses.

4. **Grid Deformation Analysis**: A virtual grid overlaid on the face reveals local deformation patterns. The method applies thin-plate spline analysis to detect non-rigid warping — regions where straight lines on the face surface become curved. Natural faces don't exhibit such local deformation artifacts.

5. **Temporal Warping Stability**: The warping field (if present) should be temporally smooth. The method analyzes the temporal consistency of detected geometric distortions. Frame-to-frame variations in warping artifacts — caused by independent per-frame face alignment — produce a high-frequency temporal signal distinguishing deepfakes from authentic video.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through face warping artifact analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
